1	# Assembler notes — not for the published document
2	
3	## A — gaps
4	
5	**A3 — an automatically-installed package on Nomad is never offered for removal.** Nothing asserts it. `AptProbe.query_target_items` reads `apt-mark showmanual`, so it holds by construction, but there is no regression test: a fixture where Nomad's `dpkg-query` lists `auto-dep` and its `showmanual` does not, asserting no `apt:package:auto-dep` diff. Unit test with mocks, trivially.
6	
7	**A14 / A15 / A9's target half — the hand-`.deb` exclusion is source-side only.** `AptProbe.capture_source_items` filters `packages_installed_from_no_repository` out of the source manifest; `AptProbe.query_target_items` applies no such filter. Two consequences, both read from the code and neither executed:
8	
9	- A14: a package installed from a hand `.deb` on BOTH machines is dropped from Atlas's manifest and kept in Nomad's, so `diff_apt_packages` sees a target-only item and emits `EXTRA_ON_TARGET`/`REMOVE`. That is an apt review line offering to delete software `manual_installs_sync` owns, and it also breaks `PKG-FR-APT-SAME` for a package both machines have. This is the one to fix first.
10	- A15: a hand-`.deb` package only on Nomad is likewise offered for apt removal.
11	
12	Both are unit-testable with mocks: give the source `_POLICY_HAND_DEB` for `code` and put `code` in the target's `apt-mark showmanual`; assert no `apt:package:code` diff. The fix belongs at capture (exclude on the target the same way, which needs one batched `apt-cache policy` over the target's manual set — the run already issues one over Atlas's names, not Nomad's).
13	
14	**A36 — a report-only package derives no repository file.** `OriginPlan.derived_files` returns empty for `UNREPLICABLE`, but the existing test only asserts no install. Add to `test_apt_origins`:`TestOriginClassification::test_unreplicable_origin_is_report_only_naming_the_origin` an assertion that the plan's `derived_files` is empty, matching the two class-1/class-2 tests beside it. Unit, with mocks.
15	
16	**A40 — a credential in an origin URL.** `ItemDiff.__post_init__` runs `redact_credentials` over `label` and `detail`, and `test_redaction` covers the redactor, but no test drives an apt origin containing userinfo through the diff. One unit test: a source policy block whose origin is `REDACTED`, asserting the install item's detail carries `***@` and not the password. Overlaps area G — leave it there if G claims it.
17	
18	**A53 — removal never purges.** Add the `test_snap_sync`:`TestConvergeRemoval::test_removal_never_passes_purge` shape to `test_apt_packages`:`TestRemovalConverge`: assert no command containing `apt-get remove` also contains `purge`. Unit, with mocks.
19	
20	**A58 — an ordinary install carries no version.** The helper `respond_to` matches fixture keys by substring, so `... --no-install-recommends pkg-a` matches a command ending `pkg-a=1.0`. Assert the exact command string instead (`any(cmd == "sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install --assume-yes --no-install-recommends pkg-a" for cmd in all_calls(target))`), which is the form the held-package tests already use via `_PINNED_INSTALL`. Unit, with mocks.
21	
22	**A60 — origin divergence takes precedence over a version difference.** `diff_apt_packages` checks `is_origin_mismatch` in the `elif` branch before the version comparison, so it holds structurally, but the only test uses the same version on both sides. Copy `test_apt_origins`:`TestOriginClassification::test_divergent_vendor_provenance_reports_origin_mismatch` with Atlas at 1.0 and Nomad at 2.0 and assert the diff class is `ORIGIN_MISMATCH`, not `VERSION_MISMATCH`. Unit, with mocks.
23	
24	**A62 / A63 — vendor-versus-distribution origin divergence is never raised.** `origins.is_origin_mismatch` returns `True` only when `vendor_source_origins` and `vendor_target_origins` are BOTH non-empty and disjoint. `vendor_target_origins` is the target's installed origins minus the target's own distribution origins, so a target copy served by the archive yields an empty tuple and the comparison short-circuits. Atlas's `gh` from `cli.github.com` against Nomad's `gh` from the Ubuntu archive therefore falls through to the version comparison — reported as a version difference if the versions differ, and as nothing at all if they match. That is exactly the case `PKG-FR-APT-IDENTITY`'s own "Why" names as two different pieces of software. The suppression's stated purpose (two machines on different mirrors) is already served by computing distribution origins per machine (A23), so the extra `bool(plan.vendor_target_origins)` condition appears to be over-broad rather than load-bearing. Needs a requirements ruling before a test: if the article is meant as written, drop the `vendor_target_origins` emptiness condition and add two unit tests (differing versions, and identical versions). Mocks suffice.
25	
26	**No VM coverage of the origin model.** The only integration test touching D-34/D-35 is `test_package_sync`:`TestAptSyncEndToEnd::test_a_package_the_targets_apt_cannot_locate_still_reaches_the_review`, which is `--dry-run` and proves only that the plan survives class 3. Nothing on a VM proves that a real install from a derived vendor repository lands from that vendor, nor that the post-refresh verification refuses a wrong-origin install. That needs real apt semantics (candidate selection, epochs, pin priorities) and cannot be done with mocks — the existing `_install_from_a_repo_the_target_lacks` / `_remove_local_repo_package` helpers in `test_package_sync.py` are the scaffolding for it.

182	- **E16** (both facets differ) — unit. Converge the both-differ item and assert both the `--revision=` refresh and the `snap switch` land, in that order.
183	- **E19** (the change group's own verb) — unit. Assert the group title and `action_label` for a snap CHANGE, the way `TestHoldReviewVerbs` does for the other four.
184	- **E20** (both machines empty) — unit, cheap: both listings "No snaps are installed yet.", assert `plan.diffs == ()` and no failure.
185	- **E29** (short line) — unit. Feed a body line with fewer fields than the header and assert it is dropped rather than producing an item with a wrong revision.
186	- **E34** (reverse confinement skew) — unit. Source strict, target classic, revisions differ: assert the refresh carries neither flag.
187	- **E36/E37** (snapd's pre-removal snapshot survives) — E36's remaining half and E37 both need a VM: install a fixture snap on Nomad only, sync, and assert `snap saved` lists a snapshot for it afterwards. The unit test proves only the command shape. Note the fixture snap must be outside `_SNAP_REMOVAL_DENYLIST`.
188	- **E41** (a warning per machine when both hold sideloads) — unit. Sideloads on both machines with different names; assert two warning records, each naming only its own machine's sideloads.
189	- **E43** (source sideload / target store snap of the same name) — unit. Mirror of `test_store_snap_the_target_sideloaded_under_the_same_name_produces_no_diff`, asserting no removal is offered for Nomad's store copy.
190	- **E45** (a held sideload name on the other machine) — unit. Nomad holds `beta` which is a sideload there, Atlas has `beta` from the store unheld: assert no `snap:hold:` item.
191	- **E49** (sideloads through a real run) — VM. Build a trivial `.snap` (or `snap try` a directory) on one VM, run a sync, assert the run named it and that both machines' `snap list` still show it unchanged. Worth it only if the fixture cost is acceptable; the unit coverage of the branch set is already dense.
192	- **E52** (a snap removal that fails) — unit. Make `snap remove` exit non-zero for one of two approved removals and assert only that item is in `PackageItemFailures` and the other command still ran.
193	- **E53** (per-item failure through a real run) — VM. The apt equivalent exists (`test_continue_on_item_failure`); the snap version needs a snap whose revision Nomad cannot fetch, which is awkward to arrange reliably — approving a hold for a snap the run also declines to install is the cheaper VM trigger.
194	- **E88/E89** (self-expiry) — E88's remaining half is VM-only and slow (the pause is six hours). A cheaper substitute: assert on a VM that the value snapd stores after the pause parses as a future timestamp rather than the indefinite literal. E89 (a run that dies) can be a VM test that kills the sync mid-window and asserts the stored value is timed, not indefinite — that is the observable consequence, since waiting out the expiry is not testable.
195	- **E99** (restore precedes connection teardown) — unit. In `_cleanup`, record the order of the restore call and the connection close and assert the restore comes first; today only the abort path touches `_cleanup`.
196	- **E113** (`~/snap` boundary end to end) — VM. Put a stale revision directory under `~/snap/<app>/` on Atlas, run a sync with both jobs enabled, and assert Nomad has the active revision's directory and `common` but not the stale one.
197	
198	## E — notes
199	
200	- **E.9 is the orchestrator's code, not the job's.** Every row there exercises `Orchestrator._hold_snap_autorefresh` / `_apply_snap_hold` / `_verify_snap_hold` / `_restore_snap_hold` / `_restore_snap_autorefresh` in `src/pcswitcher/orchestrator.py` — there is no separate module. If area K (orchestration ordering) also claims the pause, keep the ordering claim there (pause engaged before the job window, restored first in cleanup) and the policy claims here.
201	- **E101–E103 overlap the preconditions area.** They are `PKG-FR-SUDO-PRECONDITION` rows, but snap's source-side sudo requirement exists solely because of the refresh pause, so they belong to whichever section keeps that causal link. Drop them here if the preconditions area covers them.
202	- **E109–E112 overlap folder_sync.** They are the `folder_sync` half of `PKG-FR-SNAP-DATA-BOUNDARY`; the source of the excluded paths (`snap_sync_exclude_paths`) is snap's. Merge with any `PKG-FR-DATA-BOUNDARY` rows another area emits rather than duplicating.
203	- **E68–E70 overlap the machine-specific-mark area.** They are `PKG-FR-MACHINE-SPECIFIC` applied to a snap hold, kept here because the hold's identity (`snap:hold:<name>` being a strict superstring of `snap:<name>`) is what makes them non-generic.
204	- **A requirements-level ambiguity worth flagging.** `PKG-FR-SNAP-SIDELOAD` says a run "MUST name the ones it found so the user knows they are unmanaged". The code names them as a job WARNING (`SnapSyncJob._warn_sideloaded`), not as a review line or a report entry. Whether a warning satisfies "a run MUST name" is a judgement the article does not settle; I recorded the rows as covered on that reading. If the intended reading is the report, E38/E39 become ‼ rather than U.
205	- **One split worth knowing about.** `PKG-FR-SNAP-CASES` names four cases; I split each into the item it produces (E7, E10, E11/E13/E15, E17) and the command that item produces when approved (E8/E9, E12, E14, E16), because the requirement's "at the source's revision and channel" is an outcome the diff alone does not deliver. Most of the unasserted halves are on the command side.
206	- **The `held`-capture-timing question is settled against a real snapd** (E71) — the source comment in `_parse_snap_list` that says "if a VM integration test ever shows a system hold flipping this token" now has that test, and it does not.
207	
208	## F — gaps
209	
210	- **F43 ‼ (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-REMOTE-TRUST`, accepted).** A remote whose key Atlas holds via the ostree per-remote `gpgkeypath` option is replicated as holding no key: `_stage_source_keys` reads only `<installation>/repo/<remote>.trustedkeys.gpg` and `/usr/share/ostree/trusted.gpg.d`. Recorded as accepted in the criteria (flatpak never writes that option). A unit test can pin the accepted behaviour — set the source remote verified with no keyring digest and no anchors, assert `_warn_about_trust`'s warning and a plain `remote-add` — but proving the real key location needs a VM with a hand-edited repo config; not worth it.
211	- **F44 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-REMOTE-TRUST`).** `_anchors_to_import` imports every anchor file the target lacks, not the one the remote actually verifies against. Unit-testable: two anchor files with different digests on the source, target holding neither, assert how many `--gpg-import=` flags the write carries. Decide first whether narrowing is even possible — libostree does not say which anchor a remote used, which is likely why the code copies all of them; if it is not, the row is a documentation fix rather than a test.
212	- **F60 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-REPOINT`).** "Declining MUST fail EVERY approved application that needed the source's URL." Unit-testable: extend the `conflict_target` fixture with a second source application from the same remote, decline the conflict, assert both item ids appear in `PackageItemFailures.failures` and both messages cite the decision.
213	- **F63 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-REMOTE-DELETE`).** The "keeping … : target still installs …" log line is unasserted. Unit-testable with `caplog` at DEBUG on `pcswitcher.jobs.base`, mirroring `TestUnusedRemoteIsDeleted::test_a_dry_run_previews_the_deletion_and_issues_none`.
214	- **F66 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-REMOTE-DELETE`).** An application reported as an origin divergence must keep its remote. Unit-testable: Nomad holds the shared reference from a remote named `vendor-b` that Atlas does not configure (Atlas holds it from `flathub`), so the plan produces an `ORIGIN_MISMATCH` and `vendor-b` is target-only; assert no `remote-delete` for `vendor-b`. This is the one branch of the "counted against what the machine actually has" clause with no test at all.
215	- **F72 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-REMOTE-DELETE`).** "Deleting a remote MUST take its signing key with it" is delegated to flatpak and asserted nowhere. Needs a VM: after a run deletes a target-only remote, assert `<installation>/repo/<remote>.trustedkeys.gpg` is gone. Cheap to bolt onto the existing filter or derivation VM test.
216	- **F82 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-INSTALL-ORIGIN`).** The post-install refusal must name BOTH URLs. Add `assert _REAL_FLATHUB in str(excinfo.value)` to `TestOriginIsReplicatedNotJustNamed::test_a_ref_that_landed_from_another_repository_fails_after_the_install`.
217	- **F84 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-INSTALL-ORIGIN`).** `_installed_origin_refusal`'s "reports origin X, which the target does not configure in scope" branch. Unit-testable with `FakeFlatpakTarget(install_records_origin="ghost")` where `ghost` is in no remote list.
218	- **F87 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-INSTALL-ORIGIN`, `PKG-FR-OUTCOME-FAILED`).** No test drives a full `apply()` in which one application is refused on origin grounds and another installs. Unit-testable: two source applications, two remotes, one of Nomad's remotes pointing elsewhere and untouched by derivation (mark it machine-specific-conflict-declined, or give the second application an origin the source does not configure); assert exactly one entry in `PackageItemFailures.failures` and the other reference present in `target.refs`.
219	- **F97, F98 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-REMOTE-FAILURE`).** Two applications sharing one failed remote, and the "source reports no such remote at write time" branch of `_write_derived_remote`. Both unit-testable with the existing `FakeFlatpakTarget(responses=...)` mechanism; the second needs the source's remote listing to answer differently between plan and apply, which the current `respond_to` table cannot express — use a side-effect function that changes its answer after the first call.
220	- **F110 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-FILTER`).** Add `assert "customremote" in ...` and `assert str(path) in ...` to `TestRemoteFilterReplicates::test_a_filter_flatpak_refuses_fails_the_app_and_quotes_the_error`.
221	- **F111, F112 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-FILTER`).** The mkdir, the `install --mode=0644` write, and the staging failure inside `_replicate_remote_filter` all produce a distinct reason string and none is tested. Unit-testable by adding substring responses (`"mkdir --parents /"`, `"install --mode=0644"`) to `TestRemoteFilterReplicates._target`, and for staging by making `send_file` raise or the staging `mkdir` fail.
222	- **F116, F143, F144 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-PRIVILEGE`).** The system-scope filter write/apply and the system-scope repoint are never asserted to run under sudo, and the user-scope unwritable-path case is untested. All unit-testable: reuse `trust_job(..., scope="system")` for the repoint, and give `TestRemoteFilterReplicates` a system-scope variant asserting `sudo ` on `mkdir`, `install` and `remote-modify --filter=`.
223	- **F118 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-FILTER`).** Nomad restricting a remote no approved application needs. Behaviour follows from derivation (nothing is touched), but the article's sentence "a remote the source does not restrict MUST NOT stay restricted on the target" is unqualified. Needs a requirements decision before a test — see Notes.
224	- **F120, F121 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-THIRD-SCOPE`).** Nothing asserts that no third installation is ever asked about, and nothing decides what a third-installation application means for the remote-deletion count. F120 is unit-testable as a negative control (assert every `flatpak remotes`/`flatpak mask` command carries `--user` or `--system`). F121 needs a requirements answer first: a third-scope application whose origin resolves to a `--user`/`--system` remote is invisible to `_target_refs_now`'s parser and so cannot keep that remote alive. Whether that is acceptable is a decision, not a test.
225	- **F136 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-PRIVILEGE`).** The "system remote alone triggers the sudo check" arm of `_system_scope_in_play`. Unit-testable: a source with only a `--system` remotes listing and a failing `sudo --non-interactive true` on the target.
226	- **F138, F139 (`PKG-FR-FLATPAK-PRIVILEGE`).** The user-scope uninstall assertion is substring-based (a `sudo ` prefix would pass) and the system-scope uninstall has no test. Both unit-testable — assert `not install_cmd.startswith("sudo ")` and add a system-scope removal to `converge_target()`.
227	
228	## F — notes
229	
230	- **Overlap with the reporting/dry-run area.** F5–F8 decompose `PKG-FR-READ-FAILS-JOB` and validation as they land on flatpak specifically; if another agent covered those articles generically, keep these as the flatpak instances and drop any duplicate. F4 belongs half to `PKG-FR-DATA-BOUNDARY`, whose other half (`folder_sync`'s gating) is not mine.
231	- **Overlap with the review UI area.** The repoint question's shape — two answers, harmless default, not promotable, not a removal direction — is enforced by the shared `REPO_CONFLICT_REVIEW_ACTION` that apt's repository conflict also uses. F58 asserts the flatpak-specific consequence (nothing recorded); the generic mechanics of that action belong to H, and to apt's `PKG-FR-REPO-CONFLICT` rows.
232	- **A genuine ambiguity in `PKG-FR-FLATPAK-FILTER` (row F118).** "No filter may be in force on a remote **this run provisions**" is scoped to derived remotes, but the next clause, "a remote the source does not restrict MUST NOT stay restricted on the target", carries no such scope. Read literally it would require clearing filters on remotes no approved application needs, which contradicts `PKG-FR-FLATPAK-REMOTE-DERIVED`'s "a remote that feeds no application approved this run MUST NOT be synced". The code takes the narrow reading. Either the article gains the scope explicitly or the code gains a pass over every shared remote; it cannot be both.
233	- **A stale claim in the source, not a behaviour gap.** `flatpak_sync.py`'s module docstring still says "a verified remote with no key material anywhere on the source is refused outright — every approved ref from it fails naming the remote". `_warn_about_trust` does the opposite (provisions and warns), which is what `PKG-FR-FLATPAK-REMOTE-TRUST` and the criteria's accepted-cost note require, and what `TestRemoteTrustTravelsWithTheDerivedWrite::test_a_verified_remote_with_no_key_anywhere_is_added_plainly_and_the_run_says_so` asserts. The docstring paragraph is what needs fixing; row F39 is met.
234	- **A stale symbol reference in the VM test.** `test_package_sync`'s filter test's assertion message names `flatpak_sync._FILTERED_OPTION`, which does not exist — the module reads the `filter` column (`_NO_FILTER`), not a `filtered` token in `options`. The test's own assertion is on the real machine's output and is sound; only the message misleads.
235	- **Rows I split.** `PKG-FR-FLATPAK-REPOINT` produced fourteen rows (F45–F58) because the article names four triggers, five things the question must do, three answers and one prohibition. `PKG-FR-FLATPAK-FILTER` produced twenty (F99–F118) for the same reason: copy, re-apply, ordering, clearing whichever machine set it, the converge-back case, and five distinct failure points.
236	- **Rows I merged.** F40 merges the vanished per-remote keyring and the vanished anchor (one rule, two tests). F142 merges the two deletion scopes into one privilege row because both are asserted by exact command string.
237	- **Test-fixture note for whoever writes the missing tests.** `FakeFlatpakTarget` models the measured flatpak behaviours the origin guarantee rests on (`remote-add --if-not-exists` as a no-op on an existing name, `remote-modify --url` repointing, install recording an origin, a filter refusing an install). Every gap above except F72 and F43 can be driven through it; extending it is cheaper than a new fake.
238	
239	## G — gaps
240	
241	**G5 — hand-`.deb` outside the manual set.** Unit test: `apt-mark showmanual` returns a set that omits the package, policy output includes its origin-less block; assert it is not presented. Mocks suffice.
242	
243	**G6 — hand-installed at a newer version than the repository offers.** Unit test: craft policy output whose `***` row carries only `/var/lib/dpkg/status` while an older row carries a repository URI; assert the package is presented. Mocks suffice, and this is the shape the parser's docstring claims to handle with no test behind it.
244	
245	**G27 — a real bare `.deb`.** Needs a VM: install a small `.deb` on pc1 with `dpkg --install`, run with only this job enabled and the automation map answering that item, assert the item reached the review. Real apt/dpkg semantics are the point — a mock cannot show that apt reports the installed version as its own candidate.
246	
247	**G28 — the scan's real-world noise.** Needs a VM: run the scan on a stock pc1 and record what it names, in particular whether `/usr/local/bin` and `/usr/local/lib` are themselves reported alongside their children (they are queried both as roots and as entries of `/usr/local`). Not derivable from mocks — it depends on whether the distribution's own packages claim those directories.
248	
249	**G35 — skip-for-now records nothing.** Unit test: drive `apply()` for this job with one unreproducible item decided skip-for-now and assert no write of `manual.decisions.yaml` reaches Atlas. Mocks suffice.
250	
251	**G36 — the permanent mark is written on Atlas.** Unit test: same shape with skip-always, asserting the write goes through the source executor and never the target's, and that the entry carries the item's own id and label. Mocks suffice. This is the only branch of `_finalize_unreproducible` with no test at all — the read side (G37) is covered, the write side is not.
252	
253	**G45 — a mark on Nomad does not silence an Atlas-held finding.** Unit test: seed Nomad's decision file with the item id, leave Atlas's empty, assert the item is still presented. Mocks suffice.
254	
255	**G47 — this job's own no-terminal skip.** Unit test: `FakeReviewer(was_interactive=False)` with a non-empty scan, assert `JobSkipped` and that no `send_file` and no `bash -c` reached Nomad. Mocks suffice; the existing stand-in-job test does not exercise this job's `after_review`.
256	
257	**G52 — the once-per-run guard.** Unit test: drive `execute()` with one written snippet and count the registry writes on Atlas (`mv --force` of `package-snippets.yaml`) — exactly one. Mocks suffice.
258	
259	**G54 — rehearsal of a pre-existing snippet.** Unit test: dry run with Atlas holding the snippet and the review approving, assert the preview line names the item and no `bash -c` reached Nomad. Mocks suffice.
260	
261	**G55 — rehearsal records no permanent mark.** Fold into G36's test with `dry_run=True`.
262	
263	**G60 / G78 — a body the tool must not interpret.** Unit test: store and replay a body containing `[bold]`, `$(...)`, backticks and quotes, asserting exact round-trip and exact replay command; and drive the registry-overwrite question with such a label and body, asserting the question renders (it would raise on unescaped markup). Mocks suffice.
264	
265	**G61 — the authoring warning.** Unit test in the review module: patch the editor, assert the console received text naming the target machine and warning that a command asking a question hangs the sync. Mocks suffice.
266	
267	**G72 — label-only difference is silently overwritten (finding).** The comparison in `_guard_registry_overwrite` is `source.body != target.body`; label, authoring time and authoring machine are ignored. A Nomad entry whose label differs is replaced with no question. Whether this counts as "changing an entry the target holds" is a judgement the article does not settle — see Notes. If it is to be treated as a change, the fix and its test are both one line.
268	
269	**G74 — declining ends the run, not just the job.** Unit or integration: the unit path can assert the exception escapes `execute()` unchanged; proving the remaining jobs do not run needs the orchestrator, so an orchestrator-level unit test with two stub jobs is the cheap version.
270	
271	**G79 / G80 — a corrupt registry on either side.** Unit tests: (a) Nomad's registry unparseable, Atlas's holds one entry → assert whether a question is asked, and record the answer as the decision it is; (b) Atlas's on-disk registry unparseable while Nomad holds entries → assert the question is asked and, if approved, that a corrupt file is what gets sent. Mocks suffice. Both are ADR-022 "bad data is handled" cases with no coverage.
272	
273	**G83 — an answered run with an empty review still transfers the registry.** Unit test: `FakeReviewer(was_interactive=True)`, empty scan, an on-disk registry on Atlas → assert `send_file` was called. Mocks suffice. This is the mirror of the covered no-terminal case (G82) and the one that shows the registry is carried for its own sake.
274	
275	**G84 — transfer plumbing failures.** Unit test: make the directory creation on Nomad fail, then make the home lookup fail; assert each raises naming Nomad and that `send_file` never ran. Mocks suffice.
276	
277	**G87 — a snippet lacking administrative rights.** Could be a VM test (a snippet doing `sudo` where the SSH user has no rights), but it adds nothing over G86 unless the message is asserted; low value.
278	
279	**G90 — no record kept on Nomad.** Unit test: after a successful replay, assert no command issued to Nomad writes a decision file. Mocks suffice; cheap regression fence for the non-goal.
280	
281	**G92 — first-sync scope wording.** Unit test asserting `describe_first_sync_scope` names this job and its mechanism. Trivial; may belong to whichever area owns first-sync scope.
282

**A62/A63** — `origins.is_origin_mismatch` returns True only when the vendor origin sets of BOTH machines are non-empty, so a package from a vendor repository on Atlas against the same package from the Ubuntu archive on Nomad never reports an origin divergence; it falls through to the version comparison, and produces no item at all when the versions match. `PKG-FR-APT-ORIGIN-DIFF` requires the divergence to be reported.

So the `apt:hold:` item survives; `PackageConverger._hold_refusal` then finds no package diff, reads that as "Nomad already has it", and runs `apt-mark hold` on Nomad for a package Nomad does not have.

**B28** — `AptSyncJob._plan_packages` builds the exact-version install pin only `if name in source_versions`, and `source_versions` skips any item whose version is falsy. A held package whose captured version is empty is therefore installed unpinned, which `PKG-FR-APT-HOLD-VERSION` forbids ("MUST NOT fall back to another version").

**G72** — `_guard_registry_overwrite` compares `source.body != target.body` alone, so a registry entry Nomad holds with the same body but a different label or authoring record is overwritten with no question. `PKG-FR-REGISTRY-CONSENT` gates a transfer that would "lose or change an entry the target holds".

The automation path returns decisions only, so `ReviewOutcome.snippets` is always empty there and no snippet can ever be authored that way.

**K82** — `snap_sync_exclude_paths()` is computed from Atlas's filesystem before the review, and is never narrowed by what the review approved or by what failed. So the current-revision data directory of an app whose revision convergence was declined or failed is still mirrored to Nomad, where snapd never installed that revision.

## Where the tool does not do what the requirements say

Every row marked `‼`. Each was checked by reading the code named; none was observed on a running machine unless the entry says so. The criteria's own [Where the tool does not yet meet these requirements](../planning/package-sync-conformance-criteria.md#where-the-tool-does-not-yet-meet-these-requirements) records the costs already accepted — the two collateral limits and the two flatpak ones — and those are not repeated here. Everything below is new against that section.

**A14 — apt offers to remove software it does not own.** `AptProbe.capture_source_items` drops packages installed from no configured repository and says the exclusion "happens HERE and nowhere else"; `AptProbe.query_target_items` applies no equivalent filter. A package both machines installed from a downloaded `.deb` is therefore missing from Atlas's manifest and present in Nomad's, and diffs as a removal. `PKG-FR-DEB-OWNERSHIP` says `apt_sync` produces no item for such software in any configuration, and `PKG-FR-APT-SAME` says a package both machines have at the same version produces none either.

**C50, N12 — a repository can be deleted while the package that needs it stays.** `PKG-FR-REPO-DELETE` counts what still uses a repository "after this run's **approved** removals". `AptSyncJob` builds that set from the plan-time package diffs — the **proposed** removals — and `diff_apt_sources`'s own docstring says so. Nothing re-checks at converge. Approving a repository's deletion while declining its package's removal leaves the package installed with its origin gone. `flatpak_sync` counts against the machine's real state after its converge loop; apt has no equivalent.

**A62, A63 — a vendor build against a distribution build is never reported.** `origins.is_origin_mismatch` returns true only when both machines have a non-empty vendor origin set, and `OriginClassifier.classify` builds each as that machine's origins minus its own distribution origins. A copy served by the Ubuntu archive therefore has an empty set and the comparison short-circuits, so the case falls through to the version comparison — and produces no item at all when the two versions match. This is the worked example the user requirements give for two different pieces of software: `gh` from GitHub's repository against `gh` from Ubuntu's archive. `PKG-FR-DISTRO-ORIGIN` makes the distribution one origin per machine; the code treats it as no origin, which suppresses more than the mirror exemption buys.

**J115 — the Ubuntu Pro payload reaches the debug log.** `PKG-FR-ESM-PRIVACY` allows only whether Nomad is attached to be logged or shown. `AptProbe.target_pro_attached` issues `pro status --format json` through `RemoteExecutor.run_command`, which calls `_trace_output` unconditionally and emits `stdout: %s` at DEBUG — subscriber identity included — before `esm_gate` ever parses it. The existing test passes because its executor is a mock.

**K88 — the snippet registry is mirrored outside its own consent.** The registry lives at `~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml`, beside the decision files, but `folder_sync`'s non-overridable exclusion is the glob `*.decisions.yaml`, which does not match it. Wherever `~/.config` is a synced folder, `folder_sync` carries the registry Atlas→Nomad after the package jobs have run — the transfer `PKG-FR-REGISTRY-CONSENT` exists to gate, and one `PKG-FR-OUTCOME-SKIPPED` and `PKG-FR-NO-TERMINAL` both say must not happen when the job was skipped.

**C7 — files apt ignores are synced as pins and configuration.** Measured on this machine (apt 2.8.3, Ubuntu 24.04): `man 5 apt_preferences` requires files in `preferences.d` to carry no extension or `pref`, `man 5 apt.conf` requires no extension or `conf`, and `Dir::Ignore-Files-Silently` skips `~`, `.disabled`, `.bak`, `.dpkg-[a-z]+`, `.ucf-[a-z]+`, `.save`, `.orig` and `.distUpgrade` in all of them. `AptProbe.capture_dir_digests` passes an extension filter for `sources.list.d` alone, so a `99-vendor.bak` in `preferences.d` becomes an always-synced write from Atlas and an offered deletion on Nomad, though apt reads it on neither. `PKG-FR-APT-IGNORES` forbids treating such a file as configuration in any of add, change or remove.

**B27 — a hold outlives its package's mark and freezes a package that is not there.** `filter_inert` drops a marked package from Atlas's manifest, but the hold sets are read raw and `_drop_inert_diffs` looks up the hold's own id (`apt:hold:<name>`) against a mark recorded under `apt:package:<name>`. The hold item survives; `PackageConverger._hold_refusal` finds no package diff, reads that as "Nomad already has it", and runs `apt-mark hold` for a package Nomad does not have. That is the bookkeeping hold `PKG-FR-APT-HELD-TARGET` calls harmful, and it blocks every later attempt to install the package.

**K82 — data for a revision that did not converge is mirrored anyway.** `snap_sync_exclude_paths()` keeps each app's current-revision directory and excludes the rest, computed from Atlas's filesystem alone. It takes no decisions and no converge results, so where a revision change was declined or failed, `folder_sync` still writes Atlas's current-revision data into `~/snap/<app>/<atlas-revision>` on Nomad, whose snapd never installed it. The function's docstring states the assumption that makes the exclusion safe — that `snap_sync` converged the revision first — and a declined or failed item is exactly what breaks it. `PKG-FR-SNAP-DATA-BOUNDARY` forbids the result.

**K81 — with `snap_sync` off, every revision's data is mirrored.** The snap filters are emitted only when `_package_job_enabled("snap_sync")` holds, and that returns false both when the job is disabled and when the sibling map is absent. Nothing unconditional names anything under `~/snap`. `folder_sync` module's own comment records this as a deliberate trade, so it is a conflict between a documented choice and `PKG-FR-SNAP-DATA-BOUNDARY` rather than an oversight.

**B28 — a held package with no captured version installs unpinned.** `_plan_packages` admits a name into `_held_versions` only when a non-empty version was captured, and `PackageConverger._install` falls back to an unpinned `install_args([name])` otherwise, so `_held_version_refusal` is never reached and the package is frozen at whatever Nomad offered. `PKG-FR-APT-HOLD-VERSION` forbids the fallback. Reachability is not established by reading the code: the empty version is a defensive default, and `dpkg-query`'s measured non-zero exit on an unknown name would fail the job first.

**G72 — a registry entry's authoring record is overwritten without asking.** `_guard_registry_overwrite` compares bodies alone, while a `Snippet` also carries `label`, `authored_at` and `authored_on`, all of which the whole-file transfer replaces. `PKG-FR-REGISTRY-CONSENT` gates a transfer that would "lose or change an entry the target holds". What is lost is metadata — the replayed body stays byte-identical — so the consequence is narrow.

**H167 — the article overstates the automation hatch.** `PKG-NG-AUTOMATION-ENV` says a permanent answer given through the environment variable writes "a machine-specific mark **or an install snippet**". `_decisions_from_automation` returns decisions only, so `ReviewOutcome.snippets` is always empty on that path and no snippet can be authored through it. `review.py`'s own docstring already states the narrower, correct version, so this is the article to fix, not the code.

## Questions the requirements do not settle

Each is a place where two articles can both be satisfied only by choosing between them, or where the text does not reach the case. None is a defect until it is ruled on.

- **A15 — a hand-`.deb` package only Nomad has.** `PKG-FR-DEB-OWNERSHIP` says `apt_sync` produces no item for it in any configuration; `PKG-FR-APT-REMOVE` says any package Nomad has and Atlas lacks is offered for removal. The external review reads `PKG-FR-DEB-OWNERSHIP` as the more specific rule and therefore decisive, which would make the current removal a plain defect rather than a collision.
- **B41 — a hold added and its package removed in the same run.** Both can be approved, because Atlas can hold a package outside its own manual set. The code removes and then holds, leaving Nomad holding what it no longer has. The articles say the hold is decided separately from its software; they do not say what happens when the two answers contradict.
- **C — the conflict question is gated on the proposed installs.** `PKG-FR-REPO-CONFLICT` says the question is raised only for a repository this run writes because an approved package comes from it, but the question must be asked before the approvals exist. The code uses the plan-time superset, so a file can be asked about and then not written. Nothing is written wrongly; no article covers the outcome.
- **D47 — a mark recorded earlier in the same run.** `PKG-FR-COLLATERAL-MARKED` says such a mark must count and that the question must say the package is marked. The protection counts, but items are built before answers exist, so the question cannot name a same-run mark. Whether the second half is required is not decidable from the text.
- **E — whether a warning satisfies "a run MUST name".** `PKG-FR-SNAP-SIDELOAD` requires a run to name the sideloads it found. They are named in a job warning, not in the review or the report. On the warning reading the branch is covered; on the report reading it is unmet.
- **F118 — the filter article's unscoped clause.** "No filter may be in force on a remote **this run provisions**" is scoped; "a remote the source does not restrict MUST NOT stay restricted on the target" is not. Read literally the second would require touching remotes no approved application needs, which `PKG-FR-FLATPAK-REMOTE-DERIVED` forbids. The code takes the narrow reading.
- **F121 — a third-scope application and the remote count.** `PKG-FR-FLATPAK-THIRD-SCOPE` skips such an installation, but an application in it can still be the last user of a remote, and the parser cannot see it. Whether deleting that remote is acceptable is a decision, not a test.
- **G79 — a registry on Nomad that cannot be parsed.** It reads as empty, so a transfer that would lose every entry counts as additive and asks nothing. `PKG-FR-READ-FAILS-JOB` says silence must not be read as an empty set; whether an unparseable file is silence or data is not stated.
- **J — a plan of nothing but report-only findings.** `PKG-FR-NO-TERMINAL` makes a headless run report any job with a non-empty review as skipped. Two machines differing only in versions therefore produce a skipped job, though nothing was ever decidable. This follows the letter of the article.
- **K23 — `folder_sync`'s exclusions depend on which package jobs are enabled.** `PKG-FR-JOB-INDEPENDENCE` says no job's behaviour may depend on whether another is enabled. The gating is deliberate and the reason is recorded in the code: a path hidden from the mirror while its own job is off is invisible to every mechanism at once. The article needs a clause either way.

content.text:
Phase 1 is committed. The document is at `docs/dev/package-sync-scenario-coverage.md`: **1,184 scenarios** across ten single-run sections plus the cross-run section, every row derived from a conformance article and every coverage mark set by reading the test rather than its name.

What the sweep turned up, beyond the coverage map:

**Defects confirmed by a second, adversarial reading** — none of these appear in the criteria's own list of known gaps:

| | What breaks |
| --- | --- |
| A14 | apt offers to remove a package both machines installed from a hand-`.deb` — the source capture filters those out, the target capture does not |
| C50/N12 | a repository can be deleted while the package needing it stays: usage is counted from *proposed* removals, not approved ones |
| A62/A63 | a vendor build against a distribution build never reports as an origin divergence — the requirements' own worked example |
| J115 | the Ubuntu Pro probe's payload, subscriber identity included, reaches the debug log through the executor's trace |
| K88 | `folder_sync` mirrors the snippet registry, bypassing the consent that gates it |
| C7 | files apt ignores by name (`.bak`, `.save`, `.dpkg-*`) are synced as pins and configuration — measured against `man 5 apt_preferences` here |
| B27 | a hold outlives its package's machine-specific mark and freezes a package the target does not have |
| K81/K82 | snap data for revisions the target never installed is mirrored |

**Ten questions the requirements do not settle** — a target-only hand-`.deb`, a hold added while its package is removed, whether a warning satisfies "a run MUST name", `folder_sync`'s exclusions depending on sibling jobs, and others. Each names the two articles in tension.

Codex's completeness pass found 15 branches nobody had enumerated, 13 rows stating something their article does not say, and 14 duplicates — all applied.

One verification round is still running on the newest defect rows; I'll fold its verdicts in, then start phase 2 on the gap register.
